articles.summary: Key Takeaways A good AR summary fits on one page and reads in under two minutes. It pairs cash-application data with renewal forecasts. The best CFO snapshot answers three questions: how much cash landed, what’s still outstanding, and what’s coming from renewals. Keep the table to five or six metrics. Each should show a current figure, a prior-period figure, and a variance. The variance column carries the report. A CFO scans it, spots the two rows trending badly, and stops there. DSO dropping from 47 to 41 days means faster collection. Cash applied rising from 88% to 94% means the matching engine is tuned. A jump in the 61-90 day bucket from $52K to $85K is a $33K deterioration that needs attention now. DSO is the most watched AR metric, and CFOs want it next to standard aging buckets: 0-30, 31-60, 61-90, and 90+. Quick Summary A great AR summary fits on one page and reads in under two minutes. It merges two things most finance teams keep in separate tabs: real-time cash-application data and subscription renewal forecasts. That pairing lets a CFO decide, on the spot, whether to push for expansion or tighten collections.
articles.title: Write an AR Summary Your CFO Reads in Two Minutes
